#13

#15

#24

#25

#28

#29

#30

#31

#32

#33

#34

#38

#39

way one thing that really stood out to me was the sense of community in the mornings you see groups of elderly people exercising together in the parks
#41

#42
be a part of it too even if just for a short while what I found fascinating is how strong the traditional values are in Hanoi even as
#43
the city modernizes respect for elders and family ties are deeply ingrained in daily life I remember one time when I was staying with a local family and
#44
they invited me to join them for dinner it was a simple home-cooked meal but the hospitality was incredible they treated me like I was part of the
#45
family and I got to learn about their Traditions directly from them they were also very proud to share stories about the city's history especially the struggles and
#46
resilience during wartime the contrast between the fast-paced city life and the Traditional Values is what makes Hanoi such a special place that sounds like such a genuine
#47
way to connect with the culture speaking of traditions I've always wanted to know what T the Lunar New Year is like in Hanoi I've heard it's the
#48
biggest celebration of the Year T is huge in Vietnam and experiencing it in Hanoi is really something special it's the most important holiday of the year kind
#49
of like a mix between chist Christmas New Year's and Thanksgiving all rolled into one leading up to tet the whole city gets into this festive mood you
#50
see families out shopping for decorations especially kumquat trees and Peach blossoms which symbolize good luck and prosperity the markets are overflowing with traditional foods and everyone's busy
#51
preparing for family reunions it's a time for people to honor their ancestors so they clean their homes cook special dishes and place offerings at Family altars during
#52
the actual holiday things quiet down quite a bit as people spend time with their families the streets are lined with Red Lanterns and there's this warmth and
#53
sense of renewal in the air I was lucky enough to experience tet in Hanoi once and it's something I'll never forget the days leading up to it
#54
are so Lively with flower markets and parades but what really struck me was the sense of tradition and how everyone no matter how busy takes the time
#55
to pay respects to their
#56
ancestors I was invited to a friend house for the family's New Year's Eve dinner and it felt so meaningful the meal was full of symbolic dishes like
#57
ban Chong a square sticky rice cake that represents the Earth filled with pork and mung beans wrapped in green leaves it's a dish that's made with the
#58
whole family involved often staying up all night to cook it the exchange of red envelopes or leash with lucky money inside is another big part of tet
#59
the envelopes are given to children and Elders as a way of sharing Good Fortune
#60
yeah and what's interesting is that during tet Hanoi almost pauses for a few days the usually crowded streets become so quiet and shops close as people focus
#61
on their family gatherings and prayers it's a peaceful time yet still full of excitement and hope for the year ahead I also love how there are tet
#62
specific games like batoma where people bet on images of animals and fireworks displays at midnight the first visitor to your home during tet is believed to bring
#63

#64
they do during this time and it's all anchored in a deep respect for tradition honestly being in Hanoi during tet made me appreciate the balance between Modern

and celebration that sounds absolutely beautiful I can really picture it the Lively streets the delicious food the calm during T I think I'm even more excited to

#69

#70
